title: Deccan College, Pune, hosts the 9th International Sanskrit Computational Linguistics Symposium in January
dek: Researchers working on computers and Sanskrit, Prakrit and Pali meet in Pune from 20 to 22 January 2027. The call for papers has closed.
body: The 9th International Sanskrit Computational Linguistics Symposium (ISCLS) will be held at Deccan College, Pune, from 20 to 22 January 2027. The series is a forum for research where computing meets Sanskrit, both Classical and Vedic, as well as Prakrit, Pali and Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit. The previous edition was held at IIT Roorkee in March 2026.

The call for papers listed topics such as dictionaries and wordnets, parsing, machine translation, analysis of the Sanskrit corpus, checking metre in poetry, OCR, cataloguing manuscripts, and software for teaching Sanskrit. Besides full papers, the symposium has a track for demonstrations and posters. Submissions have closed.

The programme committee chairs are Brendan Gillon of McGill University and Arnab Bhattacharya of IIT Kanpur, and the organising chair is Prasad Joshi. The steering committee includes Amba Kulkarni, Gérard Huet, Malhar Kulkarni, Oliver Hellwig, Pawan Goyal and Peter Scharf.
Details of registration and the programme will appear on the symposium's website.
